ai_and_data_analysis.note: Do not assume every AI/data workload uses the GPU. Distinguish model VRAM fit from overall runtime and CPU/RAM/SSD bottlenecks.

gpu_candidate_roles.gpu-rtx5070-12gb: Balanced first choice for gaming, game creation and general use; 12GB VRAM clears the project's preferred VRAM threshold.
gpu_candidate_roles.gpu-rtx5060ti-16gb: VRAM-capacity alternative for larger textures/assets and local-AI models that fit in 16GB; do not assume it beats RTX 5070 in gaming performance.
gpu_candidate_roles.gpu-rtx5070ti-16gb: Performance dark horse for higher gaming/render headroom with 16GB VRAM; only promote if the full build price, PSU/cable, dimensions and case clearance are verified.
gpu_candidate_roles.gpu-rtx5070-12gb-msi-ventus2x: Stockout fallback SKU for the RTX 5070 12GB tier. Same GPU class, but exact board size, cooling, power connector, stock and checkout must be revalidated; not assumed interchangeable by model name alone.

ranking_rules: Evaluate playing games and creating games as separate high-priority workloads; do not reduce the recommendation to FPS alone.
For game creation, score engine/editor responsiveness, project build/compile behavior, VRAM, system RAM, SSD capacity, thermals and simultaneous IDE/browser/tests.
Score 64GB RAM and 2TB SSD as preferences only when those exact capacities are included at purchase and the all-in budget is verified; no assumed future upgrades.
Treat full Unreal Engine source compilation without distributed build as a distinct high-core-count workload; do not claim the 8-core Ryzen 7 9700X is optimal for that special case.
Never claim measured game FPS or compile times without a source-backed benchmark matching the actual CPU/GPU/RAM, engine version and settings.
Treat schoolwork, research, browser/PDF/document work and general multitasking as a first-class workload alongside gaming and game development.

Treat Python analytics, larger simulations, sports/stock/BTC predictions, automated tests and feasible local AI as first-class workloads; score CPU, RAM, VRAM, SSD and long-run thermal behavior by workload instead of GPU-only ranking.
Prefer 64GB RAM and 2TB SSD only when a complete as-purchased build fits the total budget and exact capacities are priced/verified; never rely on post-purchase upgrades.
Prioritize a balanced workstation/gaming build; do not overspend on GPU at the expense of memory and storage needs for study, development and data work.

Optimize hardware and the study workflow together: daily lesson -> school test -> first-seen/application practice -> verified faculty-specific admissions mapping -> error log -> delayed retesting. Separate verified official past papers from original practice questions.

Treat the hardware study score as PC suitability, not a prediction of grades or admissions outcomes. Do not store personal school identity, student IDs, grades or non-public test materials in public GitHub.

study_and_research.evaluation_note: School learning is a first-class use case: record each lesson, base school-test exercises on supplied class materials, build first-seen and multi-unit transfer questions, map applicability to the selected Waseda/Kyushu faculty/route/year using official sources, record errors, and verify delayed retrieval. Do not claim every lesson directly appears on every target faculty exam. Unknown faculty/exam-year requirements remain unknown. Learning quality depends on source fidelity, practice and feedback, not GPU power alone; prioritize CPU responsiveness, RAM, SSD and multitasking without overspending on GPU.

analysis_and_automation.note: Free/open-source tools and local processing are preferred where practical. Do not assume paid APIs, cloud GPUs, paid data services or subscription services. Do not claim a GPU accelerates CPU-only workloads automatically. Do not add peripheral audio hardware to the required build unless the user explicitly changes scope.
